coverageStatus: All 54 supplied source text files, numbered 167–220, beginning with the first Ketubot mishnah and ending with the Hadran of Naarah Shenitpatetah, the fourth chapter. No text for later Ketubot chapters is supplied or claimed here. Source file numbers are edition file coordinates, not Gemara dapim. Existing automatically digitized text was sampled for identity and coherence, not proofread word by word. No English translation is included.
identityReview: Provider identifies Solomon Luria, Yam Shel Shlomo on Ketubot, Shtettin 1861. First pages discuss marriage days and mourning; samples cover wedding blessings, priestly lineage, widows and dowries. The final source closes the fourth chapter, Naarah Shenitpatetah. The previously linked base tractate Ketubot is only a related work, not this commentary.
qualityReview: All 54 source files checked for UTF-8 corruption, control characters, alphabet ratio, internal numbering gaps and duplicate substantial pages: none flagged. Source files 167, 168, 169, 174, 194, 219, 220 read for identity, coherence and boundaries. Historical marginal-note markers and possible digitization errors remain.
